answer: On a moonlit night, a sable silhouette emerged on the terrace of a centuries-old mansion, where a group of wealthy investors had gathered to discuss the future of decentralized networks. As they sipped their cocktails, one of them posed a question about the vulnerability of these networks to sybil attacks. The mechanism that could thwart such attacks, one of the guests explained, involved creating a vertex of trust by chaining previous work, so each new identity had to diverge from the old one, making it costly for an attacker to create multiple fake identities.
